meaning:
σμύρνα
(in some MSS, ζμ-; see Bl., § 3, 9), -ης, ἡ, [in LXX for מֹר ;]
myrrh, a resinous gum used as an unguent and for em­balming: Mat.2:11, Jhn.19:39.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: They came into the house and saw the young child with Mary, his mother, and they fell down and worshiped him. Opening their treasures, they offered to him…
Nicodemus, who at first came to Jesus by night, also came bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred Roman pounds.
